title: What the architecture gives you.
lede: Each claim is supported by the shape of the system, not by maintenance promises.

blocks.title: Manifest portability across tiers.
blocks.leadHtml: The same Application manifest is designed to run from local dev (k3d) through a single VDS, multi-node clusters, bare metal, and hyperscalers — without rewrites. Not “we tested in a few environments” — a structural property: one CUE schema, one operator, one ResourceClaim contract. Only the backing changes.
blocks.detail: Today it runs on local dev and Tier 1 (single VDS). Tier 2 (multi-node) ships in Phase 3; Tier 3 in Phase 5+, Tier 4 in Phase 6+.

blocks.title: Replayable audit log out of the box.
blocks.leadHtml: The control plane runs on kine + NATS JetStream, which means every platform operation can be replayed from the event log. Not a separate audit pipeline, not an add-on to etcd. Compliance-friendly architecturally, not by promise. A competitor would have to swap out their control plane storage layer to match — a major architectural commitment.
blocks.detail: Ships in Phase 3 (Tier 2+). Today Tier 1 uses kine + SQLite; the replayable log arrives with the kine + NATS control plane in Phase 3.

blocks.title: Managed → self-host: trivial exit.
blocks.leadHtml: An architectural consequence of how we run Managed: only the UI and operations layer is hosted by us. Your cluster always stays with you. Other managed platforms keep workloads on their infrastructure — replicating our model would conflict with their incentive structure. Workloads-live-with-us is how the dominant model monetizes; we monetize differently.
blocks.detail: Full CLI in Phase 4. Principle in place from Phase 1.

blocks.title: Six platform services through one typed primitive.
blocks.leadHtml: Not a Helm wrapper over Postgres. A standardized CRD contract via ResourceClaim and ServiceProvider, which means a drop-in replacement (Postgres → AlloyDB, Redis → Valkey, S3 → Garage) is a container-level swap of the ServiceProvider — not an application rewrite. Competitors who expose services through Helm values would have to change their resource model from the ground up.
blocks.detail: Works today: Postgres, Redis, block storage (Phase 2). Coming: ClickHouse, S3, notifications (Phase 3+).

blocks.title: Agentic operations with structural safety.
blocks.leadHtml: An AI agent can deploy, scale, restart, or migrate your apps through the MCP server — every destructive operation is gated by a MigrationPlan CRD with explicit human approval. Not a soft API check that an agent can bypass. The classifier runs in the operator: delete_app prod creates a MigrationPlan in your cluster, pauses, waits for apprafter migration approve. A competitor without a CRD-based primitive would have to bolt safety on as a side-channel, which agents can route around.
blocks.detail: Works today via CLI approvals. Backstage MigrationPlan plugin coming Phase 4+ (post-launch first bundle).
